title: Masks and clipping paths (intro)
learningObjectives: Explain masks and clipping paths (intro) and apply the visual effect with a usable fallback.

understand.concept: clip-path defines a clipping region that controls which parts of an element are visible. CSS masking uses mask properties to control visibility with an image or gradient mask. Clipping changes the visible shape; masking can use partial transparency.
understand.whyItMatters: Clipping and masking can hide content or affect hit testing and visual affordances. Keep essential text and controls understandable, and provide a conventional presentation when effects are unsupported.
understand.analogy: A clip path is like a stencil that defines the visible shape; a mask is like a transparency layer that controls how much of the content shows.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual painting, clipping, and media behaviour follow CSS rendering rules.

explain.narrative: The card is visible only within the polygonal clipping region. The text remains real HTML content.

examples.explanation: The card is visible only within the polygonal clipping region. The text remains real HTML content.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered visual example demonstrating the CSS effect.

practise.guidedTask: Create a clipped badge and compare it with a gradient mask. Ensure the shape does not hide focus outlines or essential content.
practise.independentTask: Create a decorative component using this effect. Test readability, responsive sizing, and a baseline appearance when the effect is unavailable.
hints: Keep important information in semantic HTML.
Test the effect on different sizes and backgrounds.
Do not let decorative effects obscure focus or text.

questions.explanation: clip-path clips the visible region of an element to a defined shape.

questions.prompt: What should accompany a decorative CSS effect?
options: Readable content and a usable fallback
Essential information available only in the effect
questions.answer: Readable content and a usable fallback
questions.explanation: Decorative effects should enhance content rather than become the only way to access it.
